title: St. Michael's College to cover tuition for some Vermonters - NewsBreak
text:
By Ben Breen No media credit provided. ,
1 hours ago
COLCHESTER, Vt. ( ABC22/FOX44 ) – Saint Michael’s College in Colchester on Wednesday announced three initiatives, all aimed to make the cost of attending more affordable – especially for people who live in the area.
Saint Michael’s said that it will cover tuition for all Vermont residents with a household income of $100,000 or less – though they will have to apply for Pell and VSAC grants first by filling out relevant paperwork, and maintain a GPA of at least 2.5, equivalent to a B- or C+ average.
Saint Michael’s College receives $120k to support internships abroad For Vermonters with a household income above $100,000, St. Mike’s will match the tuition and fees they’d have to pay at UVM, after institutional scholarships.
Finally, they said that any students living within 35 miles of the college and commute to campus will pay just $11,500 a year in tuition. The standard tuition at St. Mike’s is $49,950, not including room and board or an additional comprehensive fee.
Report: gaps in Vermont special education driving higher costs “We know our students get a world-class education at Saint Michael’s College, and we want to ensure this experience is accessible to any student who would thrive here,” said Richard Plumb, Saint Michael’s College President.
The new tuition rates will be available as early as the spring of 2026.
Saint Michael’s College is a Catholic college founded in 1904. They are the only college founded by the Society of Saint Edmund, an order of priests with a commitment to social justice.
More information on the new financial aid initiatives at St. Mike’s is available at the college’s website .
